key_insight: PINN-LPCDD makes PINNs viable for compressible multi-medium flows by learning interface locations while enforcing physically consistent sharp domain decomposition.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-aware surrogate for shock–interface problems in multi-material CFD, especially when media have very different stiffness and pressure levels.
method: Separate sub-networks are assigned to each medium and their interface positions are learned end-to-end.
A sharp interface method is embedded so the contact discontinuity remains physically consistent and sharp.
Euler equations with artificial viscosity and scaling invariance are used to improve robustness for shocks and high pressure ratios.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 cases, with acceptable accuracy across these multi-medium scenarios.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on stable interface learning and careful tuning of artificial viscosity/scaling for strongly discontinuous flows.
paper_title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
